text:
Dear Dr. Mercer,

Thank you for agreeing to evaluate this 12-year-old girl who first presented at three months of age with profound growth failure and poor weight gain. She was born with a birth weight below the tenth percentile for gestational age, and her stature has consistently remained far below the first percentile. Reassuringly, her milestones have been appropriate, with no global developmental delay.

She currently exhibits advanced stage four chronic renal impairment (estimated GFR 20 mL/min/1.73m²), although she has not progressed to stage five disease. Her serum creatinine remains persistently high at 2.2 mg/dL. Metabolic evaluation is notable for elevated serum potassium, high serum uric acid, and marked urinary sodium wasting that necessitates daily salt supplementation. Her serum aldosterone concentration is inappropriately low, yet plasma renin levels remain completely within the normal reference range. She has had no episodes of clinical gout. Urinalysis reveals no detectable protein in the urine.

Complete blood counts show a reduced absolute neutrophil count of 0.8 x 10^9/L, but she has suffered no recurrent infections, and her quantitative IgG, IgA, and IgM levels are entirely normal. Physical examination is otherwise unremarkable; her vital signs are stable, and she takes only oral sodium chloride. 

Her previous renal biopsy demonstrated widespread global sclerosis across the glomeruli, accompanied by marked interstitial fibrosis and tubular atrophy. Electron microscopy identified significant capillary basement membrane thickening along with extensive effacement of visceral epithelial foot processes.

Given this complex presentation, I would greatly appreciate your assessment and recommendations for her ongoing management.

Sincerely,  
Dr. Eleanor Vance
